content:
I'd like to announce leanprover/lp: verified linear programming in Lean 4.

  • A verified solver: solveVerified returns proof-carrying results (.optimal x h with h a feasibility-and-optimality proof, likewise for infeasibility and unboundedness), intended for use directly in other algorithms.
  • A tactic frontend lp, covering a similar class of goals to Mathlib's linarith (including strict inequalities and ≠ goals, and lp [t₁, …] for extra facts), plus a Π₂ (∃∀) fragment of quantified goals that linarith doesn't touch.
  • A maximize e tactic that computes a certified upper bound for e and adds it as a hypothesis; maximize h : e ≤ L names both a let L := ... for the bound, and added hypothesis h.

The external solver is an untrusted oracle. Its exact rational certificates are checked by a pure-Lean verifier, and the tactic rebuilds an ordinary kernel proof term from the Farkas multipliers.

There are no Lean dependencies beyond core (in particular, no Mathlib). The default backend compiles vendored SoPlex, which is very capable on large problems. There's also a pure-Lean simplex backend without any native dependencies, and an experimental JSON backend for driving any external solver that speaks its documented wire contract. Adding

[[require]]
name = "LP"
git = "https://github.com/leanprover/lp"
rev = "main"

to your lakefile.toml provides both the SoPlex backend and the tactic. See the README if you want a different backend.

lp handles ℚ, ℤ, ℕ, and Dyadic goals out of the box (but without integrality arguments: for that use cutsat), and ℝ once Mathlib's instances are imported. A fun quantified example:

import LP

example : ∃ x : Rat, 0 ≤ x ∧ x ≤ 3 ∧ ∀ y : Rat, x ≤ y → y ≤ 5 → y ≤ 2 * x := by lp

which Mathlib's linarith can't do, and also significantly bigger problems of this shape. However it's not a drop-in replacement for linarith (which includes quite a lot of "convenient" pre-processing that is hard to specify).

On dense ℚ problems lp is 2–3× faster than linarith (see the benchmark suite), and the native carriers (ℤ, ℕ, Dyadic) are faster still.
